contribution.value: Builds a theoretical roofline-style model for LLM inference economics that jointly handles arithmetic, memory bandwidth, network bandwidth and latency, and uses it to compute serial-speed versus cost-per-token Pareto frontiers for popular models on H100 hardware.

ev.quote: We develop a theoretical model that addresses the economic trade-off between cost per token versus serial token generation speed when deploying LLMs for inference at scale. Our model takes into account arithmetic, memory bandwidth, network bandwidth and latency constraints

key_results.value: Optimal serial-decoding token latency for dense models follows an inverse-square-root law in parameter count: token latency ∝ √N_param.

ev.quote: token-to-token latency ∝ √N_param

key_results.value: Speculative decoding at α=0.8 acceptance gives Llama 3 70B 66% higher throughput and roughly doubles Llama 3.1 405B throughput at fixed cost per token.

ev.quote: the gains from speculative decoding at an 80% token acceptance rate are substantial: a 66% increase in throughput for Llama 3 70B and a doubling of throughput for Llama 3.1 405B at a fixed cost per token

key_results.value: Maximum tokens/sec on H100 SXM with speculative decoding: Mixtral 8x22B 199 (125 GPUs), Llama 3 70B-8bit 189 (24), Llama 3.1 405B-8bit 122 (48), DeepSeek-V3-8bit 215 (14), GPT-4 16-bit 106 (460).

strengths.value: Provides the first published roofline-style economic model for LLM inference that combines arithmetic, memory bandwidth, network bandwidth and latency in one framework.

ev.quote: there's no equivalent to the "roofline model" in the literature about LLM inference right now

strengths.value: Predictions match empirical API data well: Pareto fronts agree with Artificial Analysis 2024 prices and speeds for Llama 3 8B/70B without manual fudge factors.

ev.quote: the theoretical model we've developed accurately predicts many empirical facts about LLM inference economics without having been fit to the data or adjusted with "fudge factors" by hand

strengths.value: Clean closed-form result: minimum token latency scales as √N_param with simple analytical optimum for instance size N_GPU.

ev.quote: token-to-token latency ∝ √N_param

strengths.value: Open-source code released for full reproducibility of all Pareto frontier and Table results.

ev.quote: The code needed to reproduce the results in this paper can be found in this GitHub repository

weaknesses.value: Network communication is conservatively assumed to not overlap with memory reads or arithmetic, which may understate achievable speeds.

ev.section: 3.4 Taking network communication time into account
ev.quote: we will conservatively assume that network communication cannot be overlapped with memory reads and arithmetic

weaknesses.value: MoE expert activations are assumed independent and uniform; this is violated for shared-expert designs such as DeepSeek-V3.

ev.quote: this assumption would be violated for the "shared experts" of MoE variants such as DeepSeek-V3. We still stick to the independent and uniform routing case

weaknesses.value: Number of all-reduce participants is approximated as √N_GPU; in practice some all-reduces involve more or fewer ranks, slightly raising real latency.

ev.quote: The approximation that R ≈ N_GPU^{1/2} is mildly optimistic: in practice some all-reduces will involve more than N_GPU^{1/2} ranks while some will involve less

weaknesses.value: Extra communication cost from distributing attention is ignored to keep the model tractable.

ev.quote: Because an accurate model of this would be rather complicated, in the remainder of this article we will ignore the extra communication cost arising from the attention operations

limitations.value: No safety, refusal, jailbreak, or accuracy evaluation; the paper measures only cost, latency and throughput.

ev.quote: We use the model to compute Pareto frontiers of serial speed versus cost per token for popular language models

limitations.value: Does not propose or evaluate a quantization algorithm; it only treats precision p as an input variable in cost equations.

ev.quote: Quantization is one of the primary techniques used by API providers to reduce inference costs and token-to-token latency

limitations.value: Hardware coverage is limited to data-centre NVIDIA SXM GPUs (H100, A100, V100); no edge or mobile devices are modelled.
KV-cache compression and other lossy optimisations are explicitly excluded from the model.

ev.quote: If we're willing to accept performance degradation, we can also compress the KV cache using various lossy methods, but for our model we will assume these methods are not used

future_work_stated.value: Extend the model with the more detailed NCCL latency calculations from the official NCCL codebase tuning file.

ev.quote: This is about the best that can be done unless we resort to using the more detailed latency calculations from the NCCL codebase. We leave this work for the next section.

future_work_stated.value: Test whether next-generation GPUs such as B100 continue the ~25% tokens/sec gain per generation trend.

ev.quote: It remains to be seen whether new generations of GPUs such as the B100 will continue this trend
